question.leadin: The Balfour Declaration supported the creation of a "national home" for members of a certain religion, which became this country.
question.text: Name this country that was invaded by five Arab nations shortly after its creation in 1948.
question.clue: A mass eviction in this country is commemorated on May 15 as Nakba Day, which comes right after this country's commemoration of its independence on May 14, 1948.

swap.leadin: This ruler's most famous victory came at the Battle of Hattin.
swap.text: Name this Kurdish ruler who founded the Ayyubid dynasty. He reconquered Jerusalem for the Islamic world in 1187.
swap.answerHtml: Saladin [or Ṣalāḥ ad-Dīn, or Selahedîn, or Yusuf ibn Ayyub ibn Shadi]
swap.clue: This ruler was defeated at the Battle of Arsuf by his rival during a larger conflict in which that rival was able to retake control of Joffa.

question.leadin: Some Westernizing efforts in this country included educational reforms under the advisement of John Dewey and the Hat Law of 1925, which banned the use of the fez in favor of more Western-style hats.
question.text: Name this country which had its borders redefined in the Treaty of Lausanne. Soon after, this country moved its capital to Ankara, though its most populous city is Istanbul.
question.clue: This country contains the neolithic city of Catalhoyuk ("CHAT-ull-HOO-eck"), as well as a possible religious complex nicknamed "potbelly hill," Gobekli Tepe.

swap.text: This conflict saw Operation Kadesh, an Israeli invasion of the Sinai Peninsula in a combined effort with Britain and France go take the namesake waterway.
swap.clue: Robert Menzies failed to end this event peacefully, leading to the bombing of troops under Abdel Hakim Amer in this event's Operation Musketeer.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Nazi collaborators in the Middle East.
question.text: In 1941 Britain invaded this country to depose Rashid Ali after a pro-Nazi coup. This country's namesake campaign during World War I saw a British defeat at the Siege of Kut along the Tigris River.
question.clue: Soldiers from this country were bombed on the "Highway of Death" in Operation Desert Storm during the First Gulf War.

swap.leadin: This polity lost land along the Mediterranean coast to the Fatimids.
swap.text: Name this Muslim caliphate that succeeded the Umayyad. Its caliphs included Harun al-Rashid.
swap.clue: This dynasty's capital had four gates spaced 90 degrees apart around perfectly round walls.

question.leadin: This man was found with a gold-plated Browning Hi-Power pistol, referencing his son's Khamis Brigade, at the time of his capture.
question.text: Name this leader from Sirte, who came to power by overthrowing his country's King Idris. In 2003, this leader accepted responsibility for the Lockerbie bombing.
question.clue: This man was overthrown by the National Transitional Council after the Battle of Sirte ].

swap.leadin: Name these largest cities of their respective Asian nations that are NOT capital cities.
swap.text: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, it flourished in the past due to its location at the end of the Silk Road. Many Armenian Christians have sought refuge here due to its position in northeastern Syria.
swap.clue: A rebuilt version of the Ayyubid Palace of Glory is contained within a defensive structure used by Seleucus Nicator, this massive Citadel of this city, outside of which Tamerlane built a tower of 20,000 skulls after taking it from the Mamluks.

question.text: An estimated 2000 to 4000 people participated on June 7, 2002, in the first ever organized parade of gays and lesbians in this city, though religious leaders were outraged. For 15 points-name this city in the Middle East.
question.clue: Abd al-Malik commissioned a shrine in this city that sits along with the al-Aqsa mosque on the site of a building sacked by Sheshonk I after being completed by Solomon.

swap.leadin: Identify these parties linked by their vigorous reactions to the 2009 Swine Flu outbreak.
swap.text: In April 2009, the government of this Middle Eastern country ordered the slaughter of its pig population. The decision angered this country's pork-consuming Christian minority, which comprises about 10% of the population and includes Pope Shenouda III.
swap.clue: The term "Jahiliyyah" or "Age of ignorance" was repopularized by a religious thinker from this country, who imagined an "Islamic vanguard" would protect Islam from secularism in his book Milestones.

question.leadin: Name the following about Operation Desert Shield.
question.text: This was the name given to several bombed paths of transportation running from Kuwait City to Basra during Desert Storm, including route 80.
question.clue: Many Iraqi forces in the Gulf War retreated from Kuwait using this road. It was so heavily bombed by coalition planes that it became littered with wrecked and abandoned vehicles, leading to its ominous name.

swap.leadin: Marwan II was defeated at the Battle of the Great Zab in a revolution named for this black-bannered dynasty.
swap.text: Name this dynasty which claimed legitimacy due to their descent from one of Muhammad's uncles. Caliphs Al-Mansur and Harun al-Rashid were members of this dynasty which succeeded the Umayyads.
swap.clue: This dynasty defeated a general of Korean descent, Go Seonji in one battle.

question.leadin: Following the successful Battle of Yamana, this caliph oversaw the compilation of the Qur'an into a single manuscript.
question.text: Name this caliph whose ascension caused a schism between his supporters and those who supported a man reputedly addressed as "mawla" at Ghadir Khumm.
question.answerHtml: Abu Bakr [or Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq ‘Abdallāh bin Abī Quḥāfah]
question.clue: Lubaina, Zinnira, and Bilal were among the many slaves this man used his wealth to emancipate , and the rest of his money went to fund an expedition at Tabuk.

swap.text: The Banu Musa brothers worked alongside this scholar, who translated the Roman cartography treatise Geography into Arabic. Another treatise by this scholar introduced Indian numerals to the Arabic world.

question.text: In 1958, this short-lived polity came into existence through the political union of Egypt and a Ba'ath led ally. Despite that ally's exit in 1961, Egypt retained this as its oficial name until 1971.
question.answerHtml: U nited A rab R epublic [or al-Jumhūrīyah al-'Arabīyah al-Muttaḥidah ]
question.answer: U nited A rab R epublic

swap.leadin: In November 1917, Pravda and Izvestia published an agreement signed by these two diplomats that was reprinted by the Manchester Guardian.
swap.text: Name these two diplomats who signed a secret treaty in 1916 that informed negotiations at San Remo. The Balfour Declaration was made regarding territory assigned to Britain under that treaty signed by these diplomats.
swap.answerHtml: Mark Sykes AND François Georges-Picot [accept Sykes–Picot Agreement; accept Sir Tatton Benvenuto Mark Sykes in place of “Mark Sykes”; accept François Marie Denis Georges-Picot in place of “François Georges-Picot”]

question.leadin: It went against the promises made in the McMahon-Hussein Correspondence, and Wikipedia alleges that it may have been responsible for McMahon's resignation.
question.text: Name this secret 1916 agreement that created British and French zones of influence in the Middle East as well as A and B zones that would be under French and British influence, respectively.
question.clue: One party to this agreement issued the Bassett Letter to reassure an ally of their territorial aspirations after this agreement was made public in the newspapers Pravda and Izvestia; that ally was Hussein bin Ali.

swap.text: A major disturbance faced by the Abbasid dynasty was this rebellion of Basran slaves. Though this rebellion did manage to defeat the general al-Muwaffaq, he would return to defeat them and sack their capital, al-Mukhtarah.
swap.clue: This rebellion that was led by such men as Riyah and Ali ibn Muhammad, and which involved hundreds of thousands of the namesake East African slaves.

question.text: 'Arib claimed to have been born into this family of Iranian nobles, who were originally a group of Buddhist leaders in Balkh. Under the Abbasids, this family became a dynasty of viziers, starting with its member Khalid.
question.clue: Harun also destroyed the power of this family after one of its members impregnated his sister Abassa. This family patronized scholars such as Geber and was influential during the early years of the caliphate.

swap.leadin: Unique military subdivisions of this province and its armies were called Junds.
swap.text: Name this province, whose armies originated the conflict between Yamani and Qaysi tribes. Arabs largely ceased to lead major military forces after an empire centered on this province was overthrown by a mawali army from Khorasan in 750.
swap.clue: Mt. Hermon is located on this country's border with Lebanon.
